target_audience: general readers of literary family drama
book_summary: A family drama about memory, duty, and a sister's promise.

chapters.name: Chapter 1
chapters.chapter_title: The Thread Kept In A Tin Box
chapters.chapter_summary: The story opens with Rakhi returning to her childhood home after years away, finding an old ceremonial thread and a letter that recalls a promise made to her brother before the family broke apart.

chapters.name: Chapter 2
chapters.chapter_summary: Rakhi enters her late mother's locked room and discovers fragments of a family history that everyone else has learned to avoid.

chapters.name: Chapter 3
chapters.chapter_summary: Arjun, the brother who remained behind, carries resentment and duty in equal measure while the household quietly depends on his sacrifices.

chapters.name: Chapter 4
chapters.chapter_summary: A flashback reveals the childhood promise Rakhi made during a difficult monsoon, when she swore to protect the family from a truth she barely understood.

chapters.name: Chapter 5
chapters.chapter_summary: Money, inheritance, and unpaid care work surface as family members argue over what duty means and who has paid its price.

chapters.name: Chapter 6
chapters.chapter_summary: As the family prepares for the Raksha Bandhan ceremony, rituals revive tenderness but also expose the wounds hidden beneath politeness.

chapters.name: Chapter 7
chapters.chapter_summary: A missing photograph points toward a buried conflict involving their father, an old debt, and a decision that changed the siblings' lives.

chapters.name: Chapter 8
chapters.chapter_summary: Nila challenges Rakhi's memory of the past and forces her to see that love can preserve truth and distort it at the same time.

chapters.name: Chapter 9
chapters.chapter_summary: An elderly aunt reveals a half-truth about the family's old rupture, deepening the mystery around the sister's promise.

chapters.name: Chapter 10
chapters.chapter_title: What The Thread Could Not Hold
chapters.chapter_summary: The ceremonial thread becomes a symbol of protection and pressure as Rakhi realizes that promises can bind people together or keep them trapped.

chapters.name: Chapter 11
chapters.chapter_summary: Arjun finally speaks of the years he lost caring for others, and the siblings confront the unequal shape of family obligation.

chapters.name: Chapter 12
chapters.chapter_summary: Rakhi finds an unsent letter from her mother that reframes the family's silence as protection, fear, and regret.

chapters.name: Chapter 13
chapters.chapter_summary: The novel returns to the decisive day their father left, revealing how a child's understanding hardened into an adult's burden.

chapters.name: Chapter 14
chapters.chapter_summary: Old financial and emotional debts are counted, but the family begins to ask whether forgiveness can exist without full repayment.

chapters.name: Chapter 15
chapters.chapter_summary: During the Raksha Bandhan ceremony, a public accusation shatters the fragile peace and forces the hidden truth into the open.

chapters.name: Chapter 16
chapters.chapter_summary: Rakhi confesses what she promised, what she concealed, and why she stayed away, risking the last trust her siblings still have in her.

chapters.name: Chapter 17
chapters.chapter_summary: Arjun must decide whether duty will remain a chain or become an act chosen freely after the truth has been spoken.

chapters.name: Chapter 18
chapters.chapter_summary: The family begins literal and emotional repairs, discovering that reconciliation is ordinary work rather than a single dramatic forgiveness.

chapters.name: Chapter 19
chapters.chapter_summary: A new ceremony is prepared, not to repeat the past but to redefine protection as mutual honesty and shared responsibility.

chapters.name: Chapter 20
chapters.chapter_summary: Rakhi releases the childhood promise and makes an adult one: to remember truthfully, love without control, and let duty become care.

all_characters.role: Elder sister returning home and keeper of the central promise
all_characters.psychological_depth: Protective, guilty, observant, and torn between truth and family peace.

all_characters.role: Younger brother who stayed behind to carry family duties
all_characters.psychological_depth: Loyal and wounded; his anger hides years of devotion and exhaustion.

all_characters.role: Late mother whose letters and silences shape the plot
all_characters.psychological_depth: Tender, pragmatic, secretive, and afraid that truth may destroy the children she wants to protect.

all_characters.role: Younger sister who challenges the family's accepted memories
all_characters.psychological_depth: Sharp, independent, emotionally honest, and unwilling to inherit silence.

all_characters.role: Absent father whose choices created the family's central wound
all_characters.psychological_depth: Charismatic, evasive, proud, and remembered differently by every child.

quality_attributes.attribute_summary: The story should explore how memory protects, distorts, and repairs family truth.
The story should test duty as sacrifice, resentment, care, and chosen responsibility.
The sister's promise should bind the plot emotionally and transform by the end.
Conflict should emerge through ordinary objects, rituals, rooms, debts, letters, and withheld speech.
